title: Reading Drill — Evaluating discounts at a cinema — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Evaluating discounts at a cinema — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The cinema manager had been asked to investigate popular screenings still having empty seats after booking in Bramley. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the share of reservations used, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a nine-week comparison, the team used ticket scans at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because last-minute film changes might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward same-day reminders. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
